subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & EU data residency — FinBank discovery
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbank.de>
Cc: Lars Becker <lars.becker@finbank.de>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & EU data residency — FinBank discovery

Hi Anna / Lars,

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for the time and for walking us through FinBank's payments ingestion and customer data flow. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: embed Redwood-powered summarization and agent features into internal analyst tools (PII-sensitive).
- Residency requirement: EU-only storage and processing for customer data at rest (for payments logs and customer PII).
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 for short completions (chat/summary), some batch workloads can tolerate higher.
- Scale: ~1.2M tokens/day expected in month 1, growing to ~5-7M tokens/day in 6 months.

Deployment modes discussed
- Hosted API: fastest path; currently support routing to EU region with logical data residency for most model calls (we detailed partial region availability).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool in our EU region — predictable throughput and logical separation; better for predictable latency and higher throughput.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and customer-managed networking — required if Compliance needs physical isolation or specific on-prem storage.

Open questions / items you asked us to confirm
1) Is Hosted API considered acceptable if data is stored and processed in EU-only regions, and is cross-region routing avoided?
2) Timeline for EU-region parity across latest open models (we flagged small model parity gaps).
3) Network requirements and VPC setup examples if you decide on Private deployment.

Attachments included: SOC2 summary (high level) + region availability spreadsheet — see attached.

Next suggested steps
- Marissa (cc'd) will propose a short technical deep-dive to map network/firewall needs and confirm which deployment mode matches your compliance bar.
- Anna/Lars: confirm availability for a 60-min call next week (technical).
- I will draft a mutual action plan if you want to move toward Dedicated or Private.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf; redwood-region-availability.xlsx
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@finbank.de>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Lars Becker <lars.becker@finbank.de>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & EU data residency — FinBank discovery

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Residency scope: Our security policy requires that customer-identifiable data (names, payment IDs, account numbers) must not leave EU-controlled storage or cross-border processing. If Redwood's Hosted API can guarantee EU processing and we can get documentation proving no cross-region fallback for those calls, Hosted would be preferable for speed/cost.

2) Model parity: We use a combination of larger LLMs for summarization and smaller models for parsing. If EU region Hosted endpoints don\u2019t have the same model versions, we need to understand the delta (latency/quality trade-offs). Please include specific models/versions in the parity doc.

3) Private option: If Hosted cannot meet the no-cross-border requirement, we will need Dedicated in our tenant or Private VPC/on-prem. For Private, please provide a sample network diagram and the list of required outbound ports/ips for egress to Redwood control plane (if any).

4) SOC2 and audit artifacts: thanks, I see the SOC2 summary. Can you also provide the log retention policy and proof of EU-only storage for backups?

We can do a technical deep-dive on Tue 13 Apr at 10:00 CET (works for Lars and me).

Best,
Anna Müller
Head of Cloud Engineering
FinBank GmbH

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & EU data residency — FinBank discovery

Hi Anna / Lars / Aditya,

Thanks for the context — confirmed that Tue 13 Apr 10:00 CET works for me. A few notes in advance so the call is productive: 

Region & residency
- Hosted API: We have EU region endpoints (Frankfurt and Amsterdam) that handle routing and data storage within EU boundaries. For Hosted, we can provide a signed Addendum and architectural diagram that commits to EU processing for specific customer projects (and show controls that prevent cross-region fallback for pinned models). Caveat: some newer model weights are staged in our global catalog and may not be immediately available in the EU region.

- Dedicated: We can provision a dedicated pool in the EU region (physical GPU tenancy logically isolated to your account). Dedicated gives guaranteed throughput and is recommended if you need consistent p95 latency and want to avoid any shared-hosting concerns. Lead time: typical provisioning is 4-6 weeks after contract and infra approval.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): For customers who require full network isolation and control over egress, we support VPC Peering (AWS, GCP) and an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. For VPC, we publish an IP allowlist and a one-page network diagram; for fully on-prem we provide installation steps and offline artifact signing.

Model parity & quality
- We will attach a model parity matrix that lists model versions supported in EU endpoints vs global catalog, and highlight any known quality trade-offs for summarization and parsing tasks. If a pinned model is missing in EU, we can propose near-equivalent versions and run a short eval on your sample prompts.

Audit/logging
- SOC2 summary attached. For backups/log retention, our standard Hosted offering retains audit logs for 90 days by default; Dedicated/Private can have configurable retention to meet your policy (we can scope longer retention in contract). I will include the specific retention SLA language in the doc.

Network requirements (pre-call deliverable)
- Attachment: network-diagram.png (sample VPC flow) and a short "required-ports-and-ips.txt" excerpt. High level: outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood control plane ips; optional mutual TLS for Private.

Actions I will take before Tue's call
- Send model parity spreadsheet and mark which models are EU-available.
- Provide the signed EU-processing addendum template used in similar financial customers.
- Share the network diagram + allowlist and a sample Dedicated provisioning timeline.

Anna/Lars — if you can send a sample of two representative prompts (one summarization, one parsing) ahead of the call we can run them against the EU variants and share quick quality notes.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-diagram.png; required-ports-and-ips.txt
